From immeasurable kalpas past, you have been fundamentally liberated. Why must you further inquire whether you know or do not know?
The Master said: "Dongshan still lacks decisiveness; Old Shending is worn out and without foundation. All you practitioners—whether you recognize greed, anger, and delusion or not;
whether entering death or being born—everything is entirely he."
Case: A monk asked Baofu, "What words or phrases did Xuefeng have that were like a wild goat hanging from its horns?
Baofu said, "I cannot fail to be a disciple of Xuefeng."
The Master said: "Who would dare say that you are not a disciple of Xuefeng?
He then cited the monk Longya, who asked Cuiwei, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Cuiwei said, "Give me the meditation board.
Longya took the meditation board and gave it to Cuiwei. Cuiwei took it and struck him. Longya said, "If you strike me..."
"Hit me as you please," he said, "but there is no meaning of the Patriarch in it. He asked this again of Linji. Linji said, "Hand me the meditation cushion over here.
Yang took the cushion and passed it to Linji. As soon as Linji received it, he struck him. Yang said, "Hit me as you please, but there is no meaning of the Patriarch in it."
The Master said: "Longya said that there was no meaning of the Patriarchs in it. Could this not be because Linji and Cuiwei were seeking his shortcomings and failed to fathom the deep spring?
Consider this: A monk asked Baizhang, 'What is the extraordinary matter? Baizhang said, 'Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The monk bowed."
The monk bowed. Baizhang struck him.
The Master said, "Baizhang, letting go and then pulling back—this monk has lost no small measure of advantage.
Although this monk was able to employ his wits and transformations amidst the flash of lightning and the spark of a flint, his crown touched the ground."
A monk asked Baling, "What is the school of Deva? Baling said, "Snow in a silver bowl.
The Master said, "This old fellow has put on his monastic robe backward!"
Case: When Master Yinci of the Tang Dynasty was a youth, while he was regularly using a mallet to strike clods of earth, he saw a particularly large one.

He struck it playfully with his mallet with great force, and it shattered instantly. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment. Later, an elder master heard of this and said, "The entirety of the mountains, rivers, and the great earth has been reduced to a hundred fragments by Master Yinci with a single blow."
The Master said: "The old master has wrongly provided this commentary. When the Zen Master struck through the great mass of existence, he did not know where his own self had fallen."
Case: At Mount Jing, there were five hundred followers, yet few were practicing Chan meditation. Huangbo sent Linji to Mount Jing, saying, "When you arrive there, what will you do?
Linji replied, "Once I am there, I shall have my own expedient means. Linji then quickly packed his bags and arrived at Mount Jing.
He ascended the Dharma hall and saw Mount Jing; just as the Master raised his head, Linji let out a shout. Before Mount Jing could open his mouth, Linji—
He brushed out his sleeves and departed. Shortly thereafter, a monk asked Jingshan, "What words did this monk just use that he immediately shouted at you, Master?
Jingshan said, "This monk comes from Huangbo’s assembly. If you wish to know, go ask him yourself.
Of Jingshan’s five hundred followers, more than half dispersed.
The Master said, "Linji’s one shout gave rise to doubt among five hundred monks. Jingshan said, "This monk has come from Huangbo’s assembly.
If you wish to know whether it was a matter of affirming him or negating him, go ask him yourself."
Case: Muzhou addressed the assembly, saying, "All of you, if you have not yet attained an entry point, once you do attain an entry point, you must never fail me, this old monk.
At that time, a monk came forward, prostrated, and said, "I, this humble one, shall never dare to fail the Master.
Muzhou said, "You have already failed me."
The Master said: "When the strings are moved, one recognizes a different melody; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn. You, the assembly present here, have not yet attained a point of entry.
If you do attain such a point of entry, you must never again bring me, this old monk, to shame."
Case: Chan Master Lì of Jīngzhào asked Shítóu, “What is the student’s fundamental matter? Shítóu said, “Why do you seek it from me?
Lì said, “I do not seek it from the teacher; how then can I attain it? Shítóu said, “Have you ever lost it?”
The Master said: "Chan Master Li asked from the standpoint of reality, and Shitou answered from the standpoint of reality.
This fundamental matter belongs to oneself; it does not belong to another."
Case: A monk asked Shitou, “What is liberation? Shitou said, “Who bound you? He asked again, “What is the pure land?
Shitou said, “Who defiled you? He asked again, “What is nirvana? Shitou said, “Who gave you birth and death?”
The Master said: "Shitou only wanted him to achieve liberation for himself, a pure land for himself, and nirvana for himself.
How could water-moons and mirror-images have birth or extinction?"
Case: Master Fotuoheshang always carried a string of prayer beads and recited three names: first, Śākyamuni; second, Prabhūtaratna;
and third, Bhagavān. As for everything else, it was just a single bowl-butt.
The Master said: "Reciting the three names brings about three kinds of retributive responses: first, the elimination of calamities; second, the accumulation of merit; and third, peace and happiness.
As for everything else, it is like a bowl falling over—it goes straight out of the triple world."
Case: A monk asked Yeshan, "What should I do when I intend to return to my hometown?
Yeshan said, "Your parents are lying in a thicket of thorns, their entire bodies raw and festering; where would you go upon returning? The monk said, "In that case, I shall not return.
Yeshan said, "You must indeed return. If you return to your hometown, I will show you a recipe for ceasing to eat. The monk then—
The Master said, "At the two times of ascending the hall, you must not chew so much as a single grain of rice.
Zhaozhou said, "When one's parents are covered in blood and pus, lying amidst a thicket of thorns, one must go back home.
At the two times of ascending the hall, you must not chew so much as a single grain of rice—what an excellent prescription for abstaining from food!"
Case: Yangshan addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you, each turn the light inward and look back; do not merely memorize my words.
Since beginningless kalpas, you have turned your backs on the light and cast yourselves into darkness; the roots of your deluded thoughts are so deep that they are difficult to uproot suddenly.
Therefore, I provisionally employ skillful means to seize your coarse consciousness—what place is there for this, other than being like using yellow leaves to stop a child's crying?"
The Master said: "I see that you venerable seniors merely memorize words and phrases when citing this teaching, thereby attempting to eliminate habitual tendencies.
Yet, habitual tendencies are not easily eliminated; as it is said, 'For every dharma established, a corresponding corruption arises.

You venerable seniors must take what has been explained and what has been cited, overturn it completely, so that the single segment of numinous spirit—the originally inherent radiance—may shine forth."
"In the lands of the ten directions, what fault is there in Yangshan? What fault is there in this old monk? What fault is there in you, the Senior Monk?
[The Master] raised the case: Once while Yangshan was herding oxen at Mount Mui, the First Seat said, "Within each of his hundred billion hairs, there are a hundred billion lions."
Zixian appeared. Mount [Shishuang] did not respond; he returned to stand in attendance.

When they reached the first seat, Mount Shishuang questioned him regarding the previous conversation, saying, "Just now you said that from every tip of a hundred billion hairs, a hundred billion lions appear—is this not you, the Venerable One? The Seat-holder replied, "It is."
Mount Yun said, "Precisely at this very moment, it appears before the fur; it appears after the fur. The First Seat said, "At this very moment, one does not speak of before or after.
As Mount Yun stepped out, Weishan said, "The lion’s waist has broken."
The Master said: "This statement by Guishan cuts off both extremes. Within every billion pores, a billion lions appear.
How do you all understand this?"
Citing a verse by a *brāhmaṇa*, it says: "When a *brāhmaṇa* dies and comes back, his soul and spirit see Lord Yama.
Having read through the books of a hundred kings, he cannot avoid being beaten and tortured. Fengxue said: "A single invocation of 'Namo Buddha'—all have already attained the Way of the Buddhas."
The Master said: "A single drop of a lion’s milk scatters six bushels of donkey’s milk.
He raised an example: A monk asked West Hall Master, "When there is a question and an answer, the guest and host are clearly distinguished. But what about when there is neither question nor answer?
West Hall said, "I am afraid it will rot away. A monk asked Changqing, "When there is a question and an answer, the guest and host are clearly distinguished..."
"How is it when there is neither question nor answer? Qingsong said, "Everyone who meets says they have retired from office; yet among those beneath the forest trees, one has never been seen.
The Master said, "They all merely turn back within the flow of words. Where there is questioning and answering, guest and host are clearly distinct; where there is no questioning..."
If there is no time for an answer, how should one proceed? "A year has passed and spring is already spent; the terraces and pavilions are filled with lush green shade. Case:
One day, the Chan Master Suluo of Heilin was visited by a butcher who paid his respects and requested that he come to his residence to partake in a meal offering.
Suluo went there with evident joy. The assembly all marveled at this, but Suluo said, "The Buddha-nature is impartial; the worthy and the foolish are of one essence. It simply can be..."
"Regarding those to be saved, I shall save them immediately; what further distinction could there be?

The Master said, "When the butcher paid his respects and requested that I come to his residence to partake of an offering, this was Buddha-nature. Chan Master Su went joyfully, and this too was Buddha-nature.
The crowd marveled at this, and it was indeed Buddha-nature. This is what is meant by the equality of Buddha-nature.
The wise and the foolish are of one mind.
Regarding forty-four ancient cases from the *Guzong*:
When the World-Honored One was at the assembly on Vulture Peak, he held up a flower to show the multitude. At that time, the assembly was all at a loss; only Kāśyapa...
Venerable Śāriputra broke into a smile. The World-Honored One said, "I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa;
I entrust it to Mahākāśyapa."
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. This is the treasury of the true Dharma-eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa.
During the assembly on Vulture Peak, there was a woman who sat near the Buddha and entered into samādhi.
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying, "Why is it that this woman is permitted to sit near the Buddha, while I am not?
The Buddha said, "You need only awaken this woman and cause her to rise from her samādhi; then you may ask her yourself.

Mañjuśrī circumambulated the woman three times and snapped his fingers once, then supported her up to the Brahma Heaven; yet, despite exhausting all his supernatural powers, he was unable to bring her out.
The World-Honored One said, "Even if there were hundreds of thousands of Mañjuśrīs, they would still be unable to bring this woman out of her samādhi.
Below, past lands as numerous as the sands of forty-two Ganges Rivers, there is the Bodhisattva Māmakī, who can bring this woman out of her samādhi.
In an instant, Māmakī emerged from the earth, prostrated before the World-Honored One, and the World-Honored One commanded Māmakī to bring her out.
This woman was in samādhi. Wuming went before her and snapped his fingers once;
the woman thereupon emerged from samādhi. Later, an elder monk asked a monastic: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
why was he unable to bring this woman out of samādhi, while Wuming was able to do so?"
Whether this samādhi is attained or not is a matter where the pivot is never complicated. Mañjuśrī’s supernatural powers were excessive;
Wuming merely snapped her fingers.
When the Second Patriarch asked Bodhidharma, "I beg the Master to pacify my mind," Bodhidharma said, "Bring forth your mind, and I will pacify it for you. The Patriarch said:
He searched for the mind, but it was utterly unfindable. Mazu said, "I have finished settling your mind for you.
Since the mind could not be found, his state of doubt subsided. "I have settled your mind; all matters are at rest. A hundred thousand *li* of sand come and go;
a staff supports a single sandal upon the shoulder."
When the Venerable Aṅgulimāla was carrying his alms bowl to the house of a certain elder, he encountered a woman there who was suffering from difficult labor.
The elder then addressed the Venerable, saying, "Venerable One, you are a disciple of the Buddha; how can you save my family from this labor?
The Venerable replied, "I have only recently entered the Path and am not yet able to provide such aid. I must go and ask [the Buddha]."
The Buddha said, "Venerable One, go then to see the Buddha and report this matter in full. The Buddha said, "Go and speak it;
as for me, since following the Dharma of the Worthy and Holy Ones, I have never killed a living being. Venerable One, following what the Buddha had said, he went to inform the householder.
When the woman heard this, she was immediately released from her confinement.
Our Buddha Gautama possesses perfect and universal knowledge; the separation of mother and child occurred at that very moment.
A monk asked Dizang, "It is not formed by the character 'yi' (以), nor is it the character 'ba' (八). I wonder what kind of character it is?
Dizang said, "Look at the footnote below."
I ask you, Kṣitigarbha, do you know? There are ten thousand myriad footnotes below. To count grains of sand and pour them into the sea is but weary toil;
it is better to instruct him regarding that which is before his eyes.
Danyuan took his leave of National Teacher Zhong. The Master asked him, "When you arrive in the South and people ask you about the matter of the ultimate limit, what will you say to them?
The Master said, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; why must you insist on having a talisman for protecting your body?"
When the true Way flows and one travels on foot, there is no need to carry an amulet to protect the body. The National Teacher truly acted out of concern for Danyuan;
it was not merely a conversation held at the parting of ways.
The King of Min presented one tangerine and one orange, each wrapped separately, and ordered a messenger to deliver them to Xuefeng.
He asked, "Since they are of the same color, why are their names different? Xuefeng then returned them with the seals intact. The King of Min then dispatched another inquiry to Xuansha.
Xuansha took a sheet of paper and covered it over [the message].
Ordinary colors have two kinds of names; paper covers cannot deceive the eyes of the multitude. At that time on the Snowy Peaks, he should have sealed it away and sent it off;
even now, the King of Min has not yet stilled his doubts.

Li Ao, the Prefect of Langzhou, had long admired the spiritual influence of Yaoshan’s Way. Although he had repeatedly invited him, Yaoshan did not go. Li Ao then entered the mountains specifically to pay his respects;
with solemn attire and the etiquette of a guest, he went directly before the seat. Yaoshan sat upright reading a sutra, paying no attention whatsoever to him.
The Prefect remarked, "To see the person is not as good as hearing of their reputation," and brushed his sleeves, departing immediately. Yaoshan, however—
The Prefect summoned Master Shishan. As the Master turned his head, Shishan said, "How can you value the ears while disparaging the eyes?
The Prefect then prostrated himself, rose, and asked, "What is the Way? Shishan pointed to the sky and then to a water jar. The Prefect said, "I do not understand."
Shan said, "The clouds are in the blue sky; the water is in the pitcher. The Prefect bowed in thanks and presented this poem:
"My body has been refined until it resembles the form of a crane; Beneath a thousand pine trees, I keep two cases of scripture. I have come to ask about the Way and have no other business."
Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar.
The Master asked about this from antiquity; pointing to the water, pointing to the sky, it was only Yaoshan. All were listeners at the Jetavana Grove;
now they are distributed throughout the human world.
Xuan Sha addressed the assembly: "Everywhere it is said that one should 'welcome beings and benefit life. But suppose you suddenly encounter three kinds of sick people—how would you welcome them?
To one suffering from blindness, you raise your mallet or brandish your whisk, yet he does not see.
To one suffering from deafness, you speak words of samādhi, yet he does not hear. To one suffering from muteness, you try to make him speak, yet he cannot speak. If you are to welcome them..."
It is not permitted. The Buddha-dharma lacks spiritual efficacy;
you have merely devised various expedients to test the master. Who has personally seen Old Xuansha? His ears are deaf, his mouth is mute, and his eyes are blind.
Sentient beings in this age of five turbidities are as numerous as hemp seeds.
While Guishan and Yangshan were picking tea, Guishan said, "All day long I have heard only your voice, but I have not seen your form.
Yangshan shook a tea tree. Guishan said, "You have attained only its function, but not its essence. Yangshan replied:
"I, So-and-so, am just like this. How about you, Master? Yangshan remained silent for a long while.
Yangshan said, "The Master has attained only its essence; he has not attained its function. Yangshan said, "I grant you thirty blows!"
Hearing the sound but not seeing the form; shaking the tree, yet remaining wide awake. What need is there to debate essence and function?
Returning home, the setting sun is bright. Danxia arrived at a desolate monastery. One night, he took a wooden Buddha and held it toward a fire.
The abbot rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha? Danxia used his staff to poke at the fire and said, "I am burning for its relics. The abbot—
The abbot said, "How could a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*? Xuanhua said, "If there are no *śarīra*, then bring two more statues and burn them.
Subsequently, the abbot's eyebrows and beard fell out.
In the desolate monastery, the weather is cold; they burn the wooden Buddhas. A mass of red flames stands before a withered bed. Their entire bodies are warmed through the long night;
how can the abbot bear such transgression?
When Bodhidharma met Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, the Emperor asked, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths? Bodhidharma replied, "Vast emptiness;
there is no sage. The Emperor asked, "Who is it that stands before me? Bodhidharma replied, "I do not know."
Vast and empty, there is no sage—this is the word of truth. "Who is it facing me?"—the mind has not yet ceased. Original radiance blazes forth, illuminating the ten directions;
from immeasurable kalpas, it has come to this very day.
Master Yunmen said: "To awaken to the Way upon hearing sound; to clarify the mind upon seeing form.
What is it like to awaken to the Way upon hearing sound and clarify the mind upon seeing form? He then said: "The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys a sesame cake with money;
when he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun."
On Mount Potalaka dwells the White-Robed Avalokiteśvara. By hearing sound one awakens to the Way; by seeing form one clarifies the mind.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, “I am a student newly entered into this forest of monks; I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, “Have you finished eating your congee?
The monk replied, “I have finished eating my congee. Zhaozhou said, “Go wash your bowl.”
He simply extended his request upon first entering; once he reached the forest of the patriarchs, his will was already lofty. "The porridge has been eaten;
wash your bowl and depart. The Master need not further weary himself with words.
A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Dongshan said, "Wait until the waters of the Dong River flow backward, and I will tell you.

Since the waters of the Dong River have no occasion to flow backward, he responded to him because he perceived his earnestness; yet, the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West is truly non-existent.
It is simply this: when the deluded and frantic mind comes to rest, it is finished.
When Linji visited Pingtian, he saw an elder sister driving an ox along the road and asked, "Elder sister, which way does the road to Pingtan go?
The elder sister struck the ox with a stick and said, "You beast! You have been running everywhere; now you have come to this."
The woman did not know the way. Linji said, "I ask you: where does the road to Pingtian lead? The sister-in-law replied, "This beast!
I have raised it for five years and still cannot make it do anything. Linji said, "If you wish to observe the one before you, first observe what they employ.
With these words, he manifested the intent of pulling out nails and extracting wedges.
At the edge of the white-watered field, he asks for the way; the snow-browed old woman strikes the plow ox. With straw sandals on slippery mud, the green mountains stretch afar;
even one who is not a man of sorrow is moved to grief.
The "Hanging Words" from Huanglong’s room: "What is my hand like? It is a Buddha-hand. What is my foot like? It is a donkey-foot.
Every person has their own karmic affinity; what is the karmic affinity of that venerable monk?"
A Buddha’s hands and a donkey’s feet are easy to see; the most difficult point is one's own karmic conditions (*jìngyuán*). Huangmei was not the son of the Zhou family;
at seven years of age, he received the robe and immediately understood Chan.
At the hut of Da Sui, there was a turtle. A monk asked, "All sentient beings have skin wrapping their bones;
why does this sentient being have bones wrapping its skin? Da Sui took his straw sandals and placed them over the turtle's back.
A numinous tortoise emerges from beneath the hermitage for a thousand years; upon its rounded shell, the hexagrams are layered one above another.
Covered by straw sandals, it has neither head nor tail—just listen to the bystanders as they determine fortune or misfortune.

When Longtan was still a layman, he would regularly offer ten cakes to the Emperor. After the Emperor had finished eating, he would invariably set aside one cake and give it to him, saying, "I bestow this upon you so that it may provide protection for your descendants.
Longtan asked him, "These cakes were brought by me; why do you instead say, 'I bestow them upon you'?
The Emperor replied, "Since they were brought by you, returning them to you—what fault is there in that? Because of this, Longtan [attained realization].
He attained awakening and subsequently entered the monastic life.
One who has received kindness should think of repaying it; taking back one of those cakes, the conditions for his renunciation arrived. At that moment, he attained a state of spiritual detachment.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "How was it before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch? Zhaozhou said, "Full of firewood, full of water.
"How was it after he saw him? Zhaozhou said, "Full of firewood, full of water."
The scholar’s doubting mind has not yet ceased; he sits at the ox-head, fully satiated with firewood and water. Ziqi did not need to cast it from yellow gold;
in this degenerate age, Zhaozhou is the one who knows the sound.
While Mazu and Baizhang were walking along, they saw wild ducks fly past. Mazu asked, "What is that? Baizhang replied, "Wild ducks.
Mazu asked, "Where have they gone? Baizhang said, "They flew away. Mazu then seized Baizhang by the nose and twisted it;
Baizhang let out a cry of pain. Mazu said, "When did they ever fly away?"
The lamp of the mind cannot be handed over; the seal of the patriarchs is likewise difficult to transmit. A wild duck flies away; he seizes its nose and pierces it through.
Nanyuan, because two head monks of the two halls were disputing over a cat, Nanyuan held it up and said, "Assembly, if you can speak, save it;
if you cannot speak, I shall kill it. The assembly had no reply, so Nanyuan killed it. That evening, Zhao...
When Chan Master Quan returned from outside, he related this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou took off his straw sandals, placed them on his head, and walked away.
Quan said, "If you had been there, you would have saved the cat."
A single stroke divides it into two parts; thus the two monks’ dispute is resolved. Wearing his straw sandals upon his head, the cat has no second birth.
When Minister Han of Changli asked Master Dadian, "How many years of age are you, O Monk? Dadian held up his prayer beads and said, "Do you understand?
The Minister said, "I do not understand. Dadian said, "One hundred and eight, day and night. The next day, the Minister came again.
At the gate, he saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera). He asked, "The Master says 'one hundred and eight' day and night;
what is the meaning of this? The Head Seat tapped his teeth three times. The Minister went to the Abbot's quarters and asked again, "The Master says 'one hundred and eight' day and night;
what is the meaning of this? Dadian tapped his teeth three times. The Minister said, "I see now that the Buddha-dharma is no different. Dadian [nodded].
Xuedou said: "What principle did the Senior Secretary perceive? The Senior Secretary replied, "Just now I questioned the Head Seat, and the Head Seat answered in this very same way.
Xuedou then asked the Head Seat, "When you just now answered the Senior Secretary in that manner, was it correct?
The Head Seat said, "It was. Xuedou then struck him and expelled him from the monastery.
The teeth cannot be contained within the lips and skin; the private matters of my house have become known to the common folk. It would not be an overstep for the Head Seat to leave the monastery;
it is only fitting that the Elder should be fined oil.
Luzu: Whenever he saw a monk approach, he would simply face the wall.
To face the wall whenever someone comes is a great deal of fuss; how can one expect the mind to open and see the original source?
For the sons of the Buddhas prior to the empty kalpa, the koan need not be raised and is naturally perfected.
Yaoshan had not ascended the hall for a long time. One day, the head of the monastery said, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instructions.
Yaoshan replied, "Have the bell struck. Just as the assembly gathered, Yaoshan descended from his seat and returned to his quarters.
The head of the monastery continued to ask, "Since you, Reverend, have consented to preach the Dharma for the assembly, why do you not utter a single word?
Deshan replied, "The sutras have masters of the sutras; the treatises have masters of the treatises. Why should they look to me, an old monk, for blame?"
When the bell tolls, the assembly gathers at the abbot’s quarters. In the Hall of Suffering, they request the Dharma from the Head Monk. In every dharma, there is originally not a single dharma;
yet if one says there is no dharma, dharmas will entangle the body.
One day, as the meal was late, Deshan took up his almsbowl and went down from the hall before [the time].
Xuefeng, who at that time served as the head cook, saw him and asked, "Old man, the bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded; where are you going with your bowl?
Deshan then returned to his quarters. Xuefeng reported this to Yantou, who said, "Great Deshan does not understand."
Regarding the "final phrase": When Deshan heard it mentioned, he ordered his attendant to summon Yantou and asked, "Do you not approve of me, old monk?
Yantou secretly conveyed his meaning. On the following day, when Deshan ascended the hall for the discourse, his words were extraordinary.
Yantou stood before the Sangha Hall, clapping his hands and laughing loudly, saying, "It is truly a joy that the old fellow at the head of the hall has finally understood the final phrase."
As for those people of the world hereafter, they can do nothing about it. Nevertheless, he was to remain for only three years.
After three years, he indeed passed away, departing with his alms bowl on his shoulder.
Those who have not realized the final word before the bells and drums sound possess only a superficial, superficial understanding.
The profound meaning is secretly revealed; Zen practitioners need not doubt it. You shall live for exactly three years; within these words, there is indeed a promise.
Whenever Master Bimōyán saw a monk approach, he would raise his wooden pitchfork and say:
"What demon has incited you to leave the household life? What demon has incited you to travel as a pilgrim? If you can speak, you die under this pitchfork; if you cannot speak..."
"Attained! You shall die beneath the staff. Speak quickly, speak quickly!
Secret-Magic (Bimā) raised his staff and said, "I test you for your original person; you have attained it beneath the staff and died, not failing this present life."
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou said, "No.
The monk said, "From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess Buddha-nature; why then does the dog have none? Zhaozhou said:
It is because they still possess karmic consciousness.
If even ants have Buddha-nature, why does the dog lack it? At Zhaozhou’s Guanyin Monastery, a gourd hangs upon the wall.
Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Xuefeng.
Zhaozhou said, "What sayings or phrases has Xuefeng spoken lately? Xuefeng said, 'The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa;
where will you all go to defecate? Zhaozhou said, "If you go back, please give me a spade as a gift."
Xuefeng: "The entire earth is but a single eye; who dares to defecate within it? I have sent a spade along; who knew it would reach Xuefeng?
There was once an ancient worthy who one day did not go to the hall. When the attendant came to invite him to the hall, the Worthy said: "I am not going now."
One day, while at the estate, he ate his fill of oil-cakes. The attendant said, "The Master has not gone out.
Deyi said, "Just go and ask the estate manager. As soon as the attendant stepped outside, he encountered the manager, who returned to thank the Master for coming to the estate to eat the oil-cakes.
He never went out of the gate; he ate oil-cakes at the manor. When the manor master returned to thank him, the attendant did not know [of his whereabouts].
A monk asked Yantou, "In the midst of the vast dust of the world, how does one distinguish the host? Yantou said, "A copper sand-pan filled to the brim with oil."
Within the dust, Bianzhu questioned Yantou: "How can the mind and consciousness ever find rest? The nostrils and eyes must both see;
it is like filling a bronze sand-pan with oil."
Muzhou called out to a monk, "Virtuous One. When the monk turned his head, Muzhou said, "A fellow carrying a board.
Carrying a single board upon his shoulders, how can one reach the realm of the Empty King?
This ancient Buddha Muzhou frequently bestowed compassion, desiring that you let go of yourself.
While Yaoshan was reading a scripture, a monk asked, "Master, you usually do not permit others to read scriptures;
why then do you read them yourself? Yaoshan replied, "I simply want to cover my eyes. The monk asked, "May I learn from the Master in this way? Yaoshan said: [The text ends here.]
If you look at it, even ox-hide will be pierced through.
If you study it as he does, ox-hide truly will be pierced through. For years laid across the desk, the meaning of the characters becomes naturally complete.
When Mazu was staying in a hermitage, he was constantly practicing seated meditation. Master Let took a brick and began rubbing it in front of the hut.
Mazu asked, "What are you doing, rubbing a brick? Let replied, "I am making a mirror. Mazu said, "How can rubbing a brick produce a mirror? Let replied:
Polishing a brick will never produce a mirror; how could sitting in meditation possibly result in becoming a Buddha? The Patriarch asked, "How then would it be so?
Huairang replied, "It is like a bullock pulling a cart. If the cart does not move, should one beat the cart or should one beat the bullock?"
Sitting in meditation to achieve Buddhahood gives rise to false views; polishing a brick to make a mirror involves even more delusion. Beating the cart and beating the ox are both equally false;
it churns one's heart and bowels until there is nothing left to do.
Yaoshan said to Yunyan, "Call the śrāmaṇera here for me. Yunyan asked, "What will you do with him?
Yaoshan replied, "I have a broken-legged cauldron; I want him to carry it up and down.
Yunyan said, "In that case, I shall join hands with the Master to lift it out together."
Why must we join hands? Simply call the śrāmaṇera here. An iron cauldron has neither feet nor ears;
beneath the wall, in the depths of spring, the shepherd’s-purse leaves have blossomed.
Nanquan, Magu, and Guizong went together to pay their respects to National Teacher Zhong.
Nanquan drew a circle on the ground and said, "If you can speak, then you may go. Guizong sat down within the circle; Magu then performed a woman’s bow.
Nanquan said, "In that case, you shall not go. Guizong asked, "What kind of mental activity is this?"

Who is it that sits within the center of the perfect circle? The woman immediately prostrates, each presenting their own spiritual capacity. The National Teacher said: "The Great Way pervades all under heaven;
it is not permitted for ordinary people to know it."
Xuansha instructed a monk to deliver a letter to Xuefeng. When Xuefeng opened it, he saw it was a blank sheet of paper.

He then presented it to the assembly and asked, "Do you understand? The assembly remained silent. Xuefeng said, "Did you not hear it said that 'gentlemen share the same breeze from a thousand miles away'?
The monk returned and related this to Xuansha. Xuansha remarked, "That old fellow on the mountain has missed the mark, and he does not even realize it."
"To see that the wind is the same across a thousand *li* without error"—the monk reported these words to Xuansha. One does not know how he missed the mark;
was it perhaps Xuansha who missed him?
Venerable Piṇḍola was asked by King Aśoka: "I have heard it said that you, Venerable One, personally saw the Buddha; is this true?
The Venerable One raised his eyebrows with his hand and after a long pause said, "Do you understand? The King replied, "I do not understand.
The Venerable One said, "The Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal; at that time, I was also included among those present."
The Venerable King Cāmara did not attend; the ancient customs of the lands of the ten directions were pure. He personally participated in the supreme assembly of the Buddha’s feast;
he was no ordinary monk of gruel and rice.
Once there was an old woman who supported a hermit for more than twenty years. She sent a young girl of eighteen to deliver food and attend to him.
One day, she ordered the girl to embrace him firmly and asked, "At such a time as this, how is it?"
The Master said, "A withered tree leaning against a cold cliff—throughout the three springs, there is no warmth. When the woman returned, she related this to the old woman (the Master’s mother).
The old woman said, "For twenty years, I have supported nothing but a worldly fellow. She then drove him out and set fire to the hut, burning it to the ground.
For twenty years I have lacked the eye; burning down the thatched hut was done in vain. The spring warmth of the third month is not much to speak of;
yet these words of truth may also serve as a teacher.
Attendant Kuò asked Dēshān, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Dēshān said, "What? What?
Kuò said, "When the Emperor summons the flying dragon horse, the lame tortoise sticks its head out. Dēshān then stopped speaking.
The next day, during bath time, Dēshān took a wooden ladle and struck Kuò once, saying, "How about yesterday’s case? Kuò—
The Master said: "This old fellow has only today begun to have a glimpse of reality.
With this single 'resting,' all clever artifice naturally vanishes. Where are all the sages? Every path lies right beneath one's feet."
Guizong was weeding when he saw a snake and cut it in two. A monk said, "I have long heard of Guizong;
having come here, I see only a coarse monk. Guizong replied, "It is you who are coarse; it is I who am coarse."
Slaying the serpent was no small matter; it was truly intended to cause him to escape the wheel of suffering. Yet the Master’s pride remains undiminished;
how could he speak such reckless and groundless words?
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? Yunmen said, "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper.
"Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper" means appearing and disappearing within empty space. "If you can utter a single phrase, the sun rises in the east."
The Lay Practitioner Gan-zhi once went to Nanquan to serve congee. He said, "I request the Master to recite.
Nanquan struck the gavel himself and said, "I request the assembly to recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the 'cat' and the 'white ox.
Gan-zhi bowed and immediately departed. Later, Nanquan asked the head cook, "Is the practitioner still here? The cook replied, "He has already left. Nanquan then struck him.
He broke the porridge pot.
While the porridge was being served with great hospitality and he was invited to perform recitations, he struck the gavel and each person recited the *Mahā*.
"The merit accumulated above must be brought to completion," he said, and then went to the kitchen and broke the pot.
Yaoshan held up a piece of paper with the character for "Buddha" written upon it and asked Daowu, "What character is this? Daowu replied, "The character for Buddha.
Yaoshan said, "This talkative monk!"
Yaoshan held a written character for "Buddha" in his hand; he asked him, "I wish for your mind to open. He simply used the character for "Buddha" as his reply:
"Originally, I have been observing the five precepts since my past lives."
In praise of Amitābha:
Amidst drifting, variegated clouds, a crimson sun hangs suspended; gazing upon that compassionate countenance, the Great Teacher, whose Forty-Eight Vows are as vast as mountains and hills.
Heavy! The scattered thoughts of sentient beings are as tangled as silk.

Hanshan composes this poem without a title; he simply wishes to depict the source of the mind. Though the source of the mind is difficult to grasp, its depth and shallowness lie right before one’s eyes.
White clouds embrace the secluded rocks; Climbing vines and flowers wind around the trees. Fenggan did not recognize you; He said you were Mañjuśrī.
Who is this Shide who picked you up? Because he picked you up, you are named Shide. Holding coarse millet in his hand, He would strike at the moon in the heavens.
Sweeping the ground indeed has merit; the field of vision becomes pure and clean. When Governor Lü Qiū arrives, he too knows how to feel joy.
Fēnggān has no human heart, nor does he have the heart of a tiger. Riding here and riding there, "this is you" and "this is I. Deep and distant is the pine-gate.
The solitary orb of the bright moon;
the Great Master Chan Yue.

He painted images of the Arhats—the manifested bodies of the Arhats Chan Yue—rendering their forms with such precision that not even a hair’s breadth of detail was lost or leaked; they were as if carved from empty space.
Squeeze it into a single lump; pick it up and hang it in the void. "Duh! Duh! Duh! Duh! Duh!

While it is certainly true that Master Bodhidharma shattered the six schools, was it not also the case that he crossed the river by breaking off a reed? The Great Way is equal to empty space; it is not...
The measure of empty space; the Great Way is like the sun and moon, yet it surpasses the brilliance of the sun and moon. One flower opens into five petals;
the fruit ripens spontaneously.
— The Sixth Patriarch Master.
At Caoxi, there were originally no waves; it was those who came that stirred them up.
The sun, moon, stars, and the myriad phenomena were all submerged, unable to show their heads.
Great Master Linji attained the essential intent of Mazu, Baizhang, and Huangbo. He brought forth from within his own breast the primordial radiance that has always been present.
Upon seeing a monk enter the gate, he would immediately shout; this is known as the Linji school. Even the Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot grasp it—let alone a stray cat.
The white ox cannot be grasped;
Master Deshan blows out the paper lamp, and before his eyes all is dark. Seizing his white staff, he brandishes it wildly and strikes recklessly, releasing the waters of the Yellow River.
Mount Taihua splits asunder; throughout the great chiliocosm, all dust and defilement vanish.
When the Great Master Yunmen and Muzhou pressed him until his leg was broken, how could he succeed Xuefeng? Within one phrase, yet beyond three phrases—stars fly and lightning rolls.
Whether you grasp it or do not grasp it, you are all dead men.
Master Zhaozhou had this to say:
"Zhaozhou speaks of Chan; it is near as it is on the surface of the lips, yet far as it exceeds the sands of the Ganges. This is entirely a mere description.
Non-attachment. A large radish grows in Zhenzhou. He personally saw Nanquan. An gourd hangs on the wall of Guanyin Monastery;
the wind blows, yet it does not fall.
Master Ciming was someone who inspired fear and drew loathing; he terrified Shending until his head shrank and his face turned green. Before the fire had even caught, the evening *can* drum sounded.
The abbot of Yangqi’s dwelling is old and its four walls are sparse; snowflakes leap upon his bed. Yet he still possesses a leisurely spirit, breaking into laughter as he gazes at the white clouds.
—Master Hong of Huqiu.
When a sleeping tiger lets out a single roar, the void is overturned; the Southern Dipper moves to the north, and the Northern Dipper moves to the south.
Donkeys bray as donkeys, and dogs bark as dogs. The heterodox paths are extinguished, and even the orthodox lineage ceases to exist.
Tianmu Wushang did not say that the former master possessed great eyes; he simply said that the former master had no path of approval. Is there anyone who understands this?
As for the robe of Yangqi, it was not transmitted to the ancestral master Songyuan. At the end of his life, [Yangqi] said: "Brothers, we have gathered for a long time. This is precisely...
Among those traveling on the path, there are some who simply cannot employ the method of black beans; they find it difficult to shoulder the true lineage.
The Buddha-dharma of Linji has reached a point of stagnation here. How painful, how painful! By this, one sees that our former teacher deeply grasped the intent of the Patriarchs and Ancestors.
The Venerable Tiānmù praised the portrait of the Venerable Sōngyuán. Elder Yǒng requested a praise for the true likeness of our Patriarch.
Whether it is a true likeness or not, it is my father’s praise; whether it is a praise or not, it is a non-true likeness that is the true likeness.
This is not praise; it is praise. It blocks and pierces empty space, severs the lineage of Yangqi, and extinguishes the school of Linji.
Entrusting it to the water of samādhi, one strikes the phoenix and nets the dragon.
The Zen practitioner has painted this portrait of the Master;

I request a eulogy that does not attempt to break the ancient transcendental barrier, yet the transcendental barrier breaks itself, nor attempts to shatter the molds of the present age, yet the molds shatter themselves.
Thus, the robe of Vulture Peak is worn out, and the words of West Hill are no longer transmitted.
A cubit of jade, a thousand fathoms of stone; an inch of gold, ten thousand miles of sand. Since neither can be selected or distinguished, Bodhidharma returned to the shifting sands.
If Huangbo were not Linji, how could he have struck him with sixty blows of the staff? Compared to the time before the Seven Buddhas, there was none of this commotion at all.
Since you are truly one of my own kindred, why need one go to such lengths to paint your likeness?

If one kills a person with a sword, the human mind does not die. If one kills a person with bare hands, the human mind does not die. Only when all skillful means are exhausted does the human mind die of its own accord.
A single shout originated with Master Ma; Linji inherited this by responding to the empty and echoing. This old man originally has no strength and cannot learn such a way of receiving.
To plant vegetable roots one must look upward; to sow beans one desires to harvest grain. There is no need to give rise to doubt or wonder. This year I am sixty-six.
It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. Beating the drum in the land of Silla, performing a dance in the halls of the Great Tang.
From the heavens above to the earth below, people are all in a daze. The transmission of the Seven Buddhas has come down to the Sixth Patriarch.

Is the Way far away? It is true in every encounter. When Master Luo looked in the mirror, and when Old Lady Li reflected in the water, their nostrils were each distinct, yet their mother-born nature was one and the same.
Whether you understand it or not, in Fuzhou they use iron coins.
Fufu the Vinaya Master commanded a painter to depict his illusory form and requested a eulogy. He posed a question, saying, "If you can answer it, I shall grant the eulogy.
Kegen failed in this battle of Dharma; Xinghua fined him money and expelled him from the monastery. "Where was he defeated in the battle of Dharma?
Fufu replied, "Today, this person [Kegen] ought to be fined and ought to be expelled. Truly a lion cub! He wrote only these words as the eulogy.
Recorded on the fifth day of the fifth month in the year Jiashen. Li Shizhen of Mingzhou painted the images of the various bodhisattvas in Miaosheng Hall;
because he also depicted my own shadow-image, I requested that Master Wei compose a eulogy for it. The eulogy says: "Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations."
The verse says:

Shadows pass by the window every day; One knows that others' frantic pursuits will never cease. If empty space were to fall to the ground and Mount Sumeru were to shatter, The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time would still not show their heads.
The moon in the water cannot be fished out; in vain one tires oneself breaking up the sky reflected in the water. At night, deep in the mountain temple, the door is opened and one sleeps;
the moon flies of its own accord and arrives before one’s face.
The human mind never knows rest until old age; when the mind rests, all things come to rest.
When the gourd upon the water can be held down, one finally believes that while the bridge flows, the water does not.
Greed, hatred, and delusion are the root of sentient beings. Sentient beings are the root of the Buddha. Without sentient beings, a Buddha cannot become a Buddha;
therefore, sentient beings are the root of the Buddha.
On the tower above, the five-watch bell has not yet struck; yet in the world below, all affairs are already in bustling turmoil. Tomorrow morning, my first meal shall be the books;
where will I find the leisure to deliberate upon them minutely?
Before the presence of all Buddhas, I pray for early awakening; within the realm of sentient beings, when has there ever been delusion? The fundamental source and original nature is the true Buddha;
throughout daily life, there is not the slightest deficiency.
Whether in a pure world with pure beings, or in a turbid and evil world with turbid and evil beings, one cannot escape being transformed according to one's nature;
in every case, it is simply this single body born of one’s mother.
Everything one encounters is entirely pure ground; on this pure ground, there is no Buddha to dwell. Zhaozhou teaches people to hurry past;
the stray cat climbs upside down upon the Bodhi tree.
Already old, I have no heart to run to the marketplace; beneath a śāla tree, I stretch out my body to sleep.
Having fully realized all that remains of this life, I shall not go to burn incense before the Buddha.
I have fully realized that all things are empty; I also deeply understand that this single body has no reality. Yet, I cannot let go of even a hair’s breadth of fame or profit.
When will I finally escape from saṃsāra?
At dawn, clouds pass by and the balustrades are damp; holding a round pearl, he stands alone.
Chanting "Namo Buddha" with every voice, the Way of the Buddha appears before him, yet he does not become a Buddha.

The fish float upon the surface of the water; the nature-ground is level. The birds enter the forest; the pathways of the mechanism are dense. Autumn arrives at the stone bed and the maple leaves fall.
Dream and illusion accompany the son for sixty-seven years.
The practitioner walks along the paths by the water and beneath the trees; in every thought-moment, there is nothing that is not the spirit of the Way. All go westward to seek the Pure Land;
the blue lotus grows from within the mud.

Contented in heart and satisfied in will, one may preserve this state forever. Amidst the flowers of spring in the imperial gardens and famous parks, beneath a single peaked thatched hut, there is a Daoist’s home where all is tranquil for years on end.
The Great Way is right before one’s eyes; originally, there is no subtle principle. When born as a human from the realm of Yang, one dies as a ghost in the emptiness of Yin.
The moon shines upon the pines on the ridge; the wind blows over the waters in the valley. The bald-headed old man Hanshik claps his hands and laughs without ceasing.
A person possesses a golden mansion, yet abandons it to busy themselves in vain. A north wind rises from the earth, blowing snow upon their brows.
On the distant road to the Yellow Springs, it is difficult to encounter the light of the sun and moon. I speak thus to you; now go and reflect upon this carefully.
The flavors of the mountains are unique; few people often know them. Wild greens combined with yellow tubers can satisfy the hunger of the day.
A light breeze turns the leaves of the grass; a heavy monkey drops from the branches of the vines. Entrusting my remaining life solely to this place, I idly read the poems of the ancients.
An old farmer plows upon the ridges; his hands do not rest all day long. Whose tomb is this of bleached bones? Flocks of crows caw from the high trees.
A single stream of shallow water flows on and on, flowing away of its own accord.
When deluded, follow others in their delusion; when awakened, listen to others as they awaken. Though nine oxen possess great strength, they cannot hold one back when it is pulled away.
The sun sets and then comes the dusk; the wind blows through the white poplar trees.
My home is not very far away. Look at the path beneath your feet: the crimson sun rises over the mountain peak; the stone ram lies within the weeds.
A hundred years in the human world pass in the snap of a finger. The wooden gate has no lock or key; white clouds come and go of their own accord.

Han Shan Composed Poems. No Titles. To Reveal Innate, Original Authenticity. While I dwelt alone in my mountain hermitage, everything seen by the eyes and heard by the ears flowed forth from within the pure, enlightened nature;
unconsciously, it took form as words. In all, twenty pieces. Written on the day of the fifth watch of the summer month in the year Wuzi.
Passing west of the bamboo field, I stayed at the Wuxiang Hermitage;
indolent in raising the *huatou*, I loathe the Patriarch. Burning incense, I am unwilling to bow toward the Western Paradise. In this empty room, idle consciousness is exhausted;
though days pass and months come, no growth is seen.

When Master Qing returned to his hometown to visit his kin, he entered our gate and first severed his attachments; why then does he travel the old path once more? In this Sahā world, cold and heat abound;
how many times has this single skin-sack been born?
Seeing off Chief Seat Qie:
Residing at Lingfeng on Mount Yan, how could I fail to see you off as you depart for Zhi Xia Temple? Our patriarch’s single broken sand pot was indeed too shabby to open one's eyes upon;
yet it was still sufficient for cooking rice and boiling vegetable roots.
To the Abbot Chun:
One summer’s effort may not penetrate it; even across hundreds of billions of kalpas, it is never worn away.
The golden crow and jade hare pursue each other eternally—do you see them atop the peaks of Yandang?
Arriving at the room of Chan Master Baoshou in Zhongshan, the rock chamber was cold and somber all day long; a layer of dust an inch deep covered the sutra desk.
For over fifty years he had passed his days in this manner—how utterly heartless the Way-man has been in his life in the world!
Eternal Archivist, you have arrived at the Pastoral Lodge on Mount Yanwang to seek further instruction.
The old man’s own illness cannot be cured; who can dispel the sickness of the Buddhas and the Patriarchs? The gourd upon the wall has been knocked down by the wind;
the staff by the bedside is buried under dust.
Entrust this to the great tree of the Dharma treasury to provide cool shade; let the single mind be released like mud. Yunmen’s one stroke was forty-nine;
Master Linji had no fundamental basis.
To the attendant Mo, he said:
"In practicing Chan, you must simply see through to the end. When you have seen through to the end, there will be no obstructions. The six gates shall remain open all day long;
sound, fragrance, taste, and touch will be constant samādhi."
I entrust a pearl from within the Tathāgatagarbha to the Librarian Ming; its numinous radiance shatters the doubts of the multitude.
Though the great chiliocosm is free of dust and soil, this is precisely when one has not yet escaped the afflictions of worldly toil.
The Chief Seat Jixi:
Huangbo struck Linji three times; Muzhou deserved three thousand blows of the staff. Heaven and earth are vast and undifferentiated, without past or present;
the fierce general does not come to sleep upon the frontier.

Shiran the attendant transmitted the Dharma through the Dharma with a lion’s roar; he transmitted mind through mind with the mechanism of the iron ox. Throughout the worlds of the ten directions there is no path to travel;
within the space of perfect enlightenment, there is a path to return.

Seeing-off Attendant Quan as he travels to the seventy-two peaks of Dongting Lake, emerging upon the waves: "After Master Lu departed, the stone screen remains. Singing several songs, he wandered for three days;
now the painting has been added with one more monk."

Whenever Master Jizian asked West Hall Abbot Xishan about matters concerning his travels or his daily routine, the master would only say that he remained in seclusion, peacefully practicing Chan. Although Xiqiu reached the age of eighty-four,
he had never held a monastery for more than ten years in total.
Entrusting this to the Treasure Keeper:

when consciousness and its objects are entirely extinguished, the original nature is spontaneously perfect and luminous. There is no difference between movement and stillness; speech is merely as it always has been.
What follows does not go beyond this; what came before was simply at peace. Sitting in meditation upon a single stone, the pine trees grow ever green.
As I see Master Ming off, within the gate heaven and earth are vast; beyond the gate, mountains and rivers stretch on. Before a single word has left the mouth, the entire world is ice and frost.
Its cold radiance eclipses the night moon; even ghosts and spirits dare not face it. This originally pure nature—there is nothing stored or retained within the breast.
Shide is my younger brother; Hanshan is my elder brother. Tomorrow morning we shall go together, with a single staff and a single flask.
To the attendant who asked, "Is this not a face flushed with blood? he replied: "This illness has flowed from the beginningless void of kalpas. He brought forth the three blows of Dongshan.
“Strike! Old man Ciming obtained Huanglong’s seal;
he sent Elder Lingshi Qiwu to take charge of the abbot’s quarters.
Do not treat this office with negligence; naturally, in time, you will see the full realization of its merit. Yangqi simply knows how to oversee.”
At the temple, he kicked out the donkey, reviving the ancestral wind.
Sent to the monk Duan:
the long and short cries of the green ape. Standing alone leaning against a corridor pillar, the three periods of time do not arrive together; there is but a single pool of cold spring water.
Not only are there no sentient beings; there is neither Buddha nor self. These short verses and long chants are merely for the sake of dispelling [distress] and finding contentment.
At midnight, the frost falls like flowers; at midday, the sun’s orb stands high. Throughout the vastness of heaven and earth, there is only Han Shanzi alone.
I send attendant Mao forth like a solitary eagle crossing the autumn sky. The autumn sky leaves no trace; amidst a sea of thousands and tens of thousands, they huddle together with empty chatter.
A black spot upon Yangqi’s robe—hidden deeply at Vulture Peak. How many years have passed in cold and heat? The day for its entrustment shall surely come.
Those who discuss the profound and explain the subtle cast off the dust of emotional attachments.
[The story of] the attendant who was enlightened when a tuft of cloth was blown upon him: why did he not awaken before the cloth was blown? Three times three is nine; eight times ten is eighty.
1. Master Yunmen had a retrospective inquiry, entrusting it to the Elder Guanding with this verse on the mountain moon at midnight:
The mountain elder sits alone upon his worn wooden bed; How many kalpas of stone have turned to ash?
Depart! A single point of numinous light illuminates the world with clarity.
To the attendant Zhi, I show that in my school there are neither words nor dharmas. Each monkey wears an ancient rhombus-shaped mirror; it pierces the darkness of the path, leaving no "now" behind.
In ancient times, all sentient beings of the great earth reached their destination.

A *weina* (chanting master) arrived and knocked on my mountain hermitage door; he was my dharma nephew, so there was no need to inquire about his intentions. Everything he said was entirely grounded in reality.
Fresh firewood is burned with its leaves intact; fresh water is drawn by striking the ice. It is difficult to meet again. This year I am sixty-seven.
I shall return and gaze toward the eastern ocean, where the sun rises as a single orb from the celestial shore.
Seeing off Master Qi: Ten thousand miles without a blade of grass; once you step out the gate, it is all weeds. For ten years he has been unable to return; he has forgotten the path by which he came.
This year the autumn affairs have come early; a cool breeze rises from the treetops. With staff in hand and alms-bag slung over his shoulder, his resolute will is no small matter.
Who would look upon other caves? Old Han and Shi of Liuyang—such is the conduct of the patch-robed monks; it cannot be sought out.
At the foot of the thousand-fathom cliff at Xuedou, the fire of yams is fragrant;
the sun is high at its zenith in the heavens. In the East Land and the West Heaven, there is no patriarch.
The Master said: "I am a white-haired old monk of seventy-five.
Daozang, whose style name is Wuwai (Beyond Things), composed this verse because of that.
Where, then, is 'beyond things'? It is a vain labor to point and annotate. Every single thing is simply 'I'; this 'I' truly has no metaphor."

Remove the single character "I," and movement and stillness will follow wherever you dwell. The numinous light pervades the entire universe; from antiquity to the present, it is free of coming and going.

Entrusted to Master Hai, Buddha hands it to Buddha—there is nothing more to it. From patriarch to patriarch it has been transmitted like the depth of the sea. Last night, the western wind shook the gate.
A fan. At dawn, there is no trace left to pursue.
I saw off the Venerable Chè as he traveled to Mount Tāi and Mount Yàn;
many requested verses for his journey across those mountains. The Venerable One is also traveling toward that region. Hán and Shí could not ascend to the Sublime [Peak].
Awaken! It is only because you are greedily attached to the seclusion of mountains and waters that you, like a great spider, sit with your knees drawn up for years on end;

in your stupor, you still do not know when to stop. When spring flowers bloom in full splendor, their fragrance fills the paths; at midday, the sun stands high and the mountain mists withdraw. When departing in the spirit of the moment, go with haste;
when returning in the spirit of the moment, do not linger idly.
Master Zhen, as you escort the Dharma-treasury:
Bodhidharma never came to this eastern land, and the Second Patriarch likewise did not go to the Western Heaven. A single ancient path has grown over with thorns;
there is no longer any Buddha-dharma to be transmitted.

To the Venerable Master Xiá, I show that the Great Canon of the Buddha’s teachings is to be realized beyond words. Behold the lands of the ten directions right before your eyes. This old monk has not many days left in this world;
I only wish for you, Dàolǐ, to have peace within your own mind-ground.
To my nephew Lingzhong Tong: The mountain scenery on this single story is fine; the mountain is indeed a "flying" mountain. Here, as a friend beyond the mundane world, body and mind are both at ease.

For several nights since autumn came, I have dreamed of treading upon the moon amidst it. Only when the words are further turned does one find certainty; the incense in the earthen burner has not yet faded.
I offer this single verse to you in passing. My mountain hermitage remains closed throughout the long days.

With my staff, I sing of the old dragon shedding its bones in the empty mountains; a woodcutter granted it to me as a walking stick, which I lean against the corner of my rope bed. It stands there, round and full.
Encompassing the myriad phenomena—beating the dog, beating the rain, and knocking on the wind—all are but inverted delusions.
Should anyone attempt to force these into two separate parts, I humbly pray that you will still partake. May you enjoy this offering.

Returning to the mountains in my old age, I have returned to the mountain hermitage. In this mountain cell there are no distracting affairs; upon a wooden bed with a stone pillow, I stretch out both legs and sleep.
Hanshan and Shide had not agreed to come, yet Fenggan arrived riding a tiger. The tiger’s nature was originally untamed, and it trampled all the green moss to pieces.
The spring breeze completes the repair. Eight eights make sixty-four.
This-Arn sings:
"I have built this hut to lodge my lingering shadow. If anyone asks whether this hut will fall apart or not, a single word comes forth—how extraordinary!"
Strange! To answer according to another’s mouth is to destroy [the truth]. Whatever belongs to form and appearance is all destruction.
Why, then, does this hermitage not perish? Six windows pierce through; there is not a single thing. The constant radiance has neither interior nor exterior.

When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm perishes, my binding of this hermitage truly does not perish. Walking, standing, sitting, and reclining within it, one is simply seeking— [The text ends abruptly.]
This is the constant realm: sometimes the wind through the pines casually raises a discourse, and the myriad phenomena all attain simultaneous refreshment.

To Master En, it is shown that the Dharma-treasure is right before one’s eyes, without change; it is only because of the depth of one's realization that there is intimacy or distance. At midnight at Huangmei, the robe was transmitted.
Alms bowl. Among seven hundred people, there was one old Lu who, while staying with Master Zhuojian, heard that the affairs of the monastery had been handed over last year.
"Who in this world knows the mind of the Master? Before his gate are green mountains and clear waters."
There is. One does not go seeking the Pure Land in the West;
at midnight, the stupa verse and the skull chant resound. The mountains are empty, the crescent moon is bright. There is no Pure Land in the West; there is only the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
Epitaph for an Ailing Elder: This year I am sixty-six. The day of my death is approaching.

Whether cremation is better or burial in the earth is better—Master Weian Guan of the West Hall said, "In the mountains of Gumo, there is a patch of uncultivated land; I shall stack stones to form a stupa and compose this inscription for it."
He said:
"Heaven has provided a single hole to hide my withered bones. When the bones decay, they become earth; the earth can produce living things.
I shall form a gourd and hang it upon the wall of Zhaozhou, forever escaping the cycle of rebirth and transcending the Buddhas of the three periods."
